title: About MACS
summary: MACS is a free public charter school in historic Micanopy, Florida, about 20 minutes south of Gainesville, with the motto "Learners Today, Leaders Tomorrow." Its mission, written into its contract with the School Board of Alachua County, rests on small student-staff ratios, using the Town of Micanopy as a classroom, individual learning plans, and close family involvement. The school is led by Director Brenda Maynard and governed by a five-member Board of Directors.

Grades: About Us says Pre-K through 6th (7th-8th 'in coming years'); homepage says Pre-K through 7th
Motto: "Learners Today, Leaders Tomorrow"

title: Enrollment
summary: Enrollment is by online application through Lotterease, with a lottery when applicants exceed open seats; the 2026-27 lottery was held March 12, 2026 and the school still lists itself as accepting applications. Selected families confirm attendance, turn in required documents within 10 days, and complete Alachua County's New Student Online Enrollment in Skyward. VPK families also need a Certificate of Eligibility from the Early Learning Coalition.
facts: 2026-27 lottery held March 12, 2026; page says applications are still being accepted
Once selected: confirm attendance and submit required documents within 10 days
Required documents: 2 proofs of residence, Florida DH680 shot record, physical within 1 year, birth certificate; VPK adds Certificate of Eligibility
Skyward New Student Online Enrollment opened May 1, 2026; choose Charter School = Yes, then MACS
Preference order: children/grandchildren of staff or board; siblings; Micanopy residents and children of alumni; Alachua County residents
Class size caps: 18 in K-3 and 22 in grades 4-7, two classes per grade
Capacity: VPK 20; K-3rd 36 each; 4th-5th 44 each; two VPK classes offered for 2026-27
Returning families re-enroll via an intent form sent each February
Tours: Tue/Wed/Thu at 2:30 pm, one visit per family
Contacts: Pam Bowman for documents (bowmanp@macschool.us); Asst. Director Kelly Minton for tours (mintonk@macschool.us)
notes: Tour contact differs: Kelly Minton on Enrollment Home, 'Mrs. McKee' (no email) on the policy page. The capacity table covers VPK-5th only, and the Extended Day fee isn't listed.

title: Academics
summary: MACS describes its learning model as inquiry-based with hands-on experiences. Students are graded E/S/N/U in K-2 and A-F with plus/minus in grades 3-6, and state progress monitoring uses the Florida Assessment of Student Thinking (FAST), with parent letters and a Star Assessment guide posted for families.

Every family is expected to volunteer 8 hours a year, and fundraising centers on a capital campaign for an additional classroom building, including the Barn Bash gala and engraved bricks for the Unity Park legacy sidewalk.

title: Parents
summary: The Parents section gathers handbooks, policies and family portals (ParentSquare, Skyward Family Access, SchoolCafe, FortifyFL). Student Services explains how MACS checks progress every six weeks and moves students who need help through intervention toward a possible IEP or 504 evaluation.
facts: Teachers assess students against grade-level expectations every six weeks
Students below benchmark get an intervention plan; an Education Planning Meeting follows if progress lags
At least 40 hours of research-based intervention data are required before a school psychologist evaluation
Further evaluation needs parent consent; the EPT team then decides IEP or 504 eligibility
IEPs cover 13 qualifying special-education conditions (IDEA); 504 plans fall under the ADA
Current Parent/Student Handbook is 2025 R1; Student Code of Conduct is labeled 25-26

title: Nutrition
summary: MACS serves breakfast and lunch made fresh daily as part of the National School Lunch Program. Families use SchoolCafe to view menus, apply for free or reduced meals, check balances and pay, and meals must be paid in advance. Medical meal modifications go to Nutrition Services Coordinator Pam Bowman.
facts: Lunch: $4.30 full pay, $0.40 reduced, $5.00 adult

Job offers depend on passing a Level 2 background screening, and the page links current postings, an online application, the benefits plan and new-hire forms.

Part time (1-2 days): $35 first child, $32 siblings (2025-26 fees)
